subject: Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE

messages.author: 163637736dcde11d
messages.subject: Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to import my genalex formatted .csv file using read.genalex.
Something is wrong with my geographical coordinates, because if I remove my coordinates from the .csv and set geo = FALSE, the file imports.
Please advise where I'm going wrong, Ive tried everything I can think of!

Kindest regards.

locixy <- read.genalex("D:/Dropbox/_PhD/r/locixy.csv", ploidy = 2, geo = TRUE)
Error in read.genalex("D:/Dropbox/_PhD/r/locixy.csv", ploidy = 2, geo = TRUE) : 
  Something went wrong. Please ensure that your data is formatted correctly:

 Is the ploidy flag set to the maximum ploidy of your data?
 You set geo = TRUE. Do you have geographic coordinates in the right place?
 If you have regional data: did you set the flag?

 Otherwise, the problem may lie within the data structure itself.
  - Inspect your data; if it looks fine then
  - search the poppr forum for the error message; if you still can't find a solution:
    1. Make a minimum working example of your error (see http://stackoverflow.com/a/5963610)
    2. Use the 'reprex' package to reproduce the error (see https://github.com/jennybc/reprex#readme)
    3. Create a new issue on https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
parts:
Hi David,

The issue turns out to be minor. Replace the 1 in the first row of your CSV with a 0.

The reason for that is because poppr will check to make sure that the number of populations you defined in the first row of the header match the number of populations recorded in the second row. It's a wonky artifact of the way the genalex format works. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian

-----

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
parts:
Hi Carlolina,

In the second row, starting with the fourth column (B4–B7 in excel) you need to put the names of the populations each size represents as shown in https://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/Data_Preparation.html#basic-format

Genalex files have a lot of redundancy, so poppr will use that information if it's available. In your case, you specified the sizes of the populations (A4–A7), but not which populations they belong to (B4–B7)

Hope that helps!
Zhian

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
parts:
Hello,

Thanks for your patience. Looking into the file, it appears that you have several entries in the Population column that do not have the "_" separator (e.g. 53asouth through 59bsouth). This is the reason why you are getting the error from splitStrata (albiet, it could be more informative... I did not anticipate this situation).

It is correct that you should use region = FALSE because region = TRUE implies that you have a separate column specifying region (and is honestly one of the more confusing aspects of the genalex format).

Encoding several population strata in a single column was a strategy we devised to make sure all the data for the population stays together. If, however, you have a separate data frame that contains these levels matched to the individual ID, then I would recommend importing that separately and adding that as the strata (after you have ensured that the order of the samples are correct, of course).

I hope that helps,

Zhian

On Mon, 18 Mar 2019 at 21:13, Zhian Kamvar <zka...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello,

Thanks for your patience. Looking into the file, it appears that you have several entries in the Population column that do not have the "_" separator (e.g. 53asouth through 59bsouth). This is the reason why you are getting the error from splitStrata (albiet, it could be more informative... I did not anticipate this situation).

It is correct that you should use region = FALSE because region = TRUE implies that you have a separate column specifying region (and is honestly one of the more confusing aspects of the genalex format).

Encoding several population strata in a single column was a strategy we devised to make sure all the data for the population stays together. If, however, you have a separate data frame that contains these levels matched to the individual ID, then I would recommend importing that separately and adding that as the strata (after you have ensured that the order of the samples are correct, of course).

I hope that helps,

Zhian

On Wednesday, 6 February 2019 04:57:42 UTC+1, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
Hi Carlolina,

In the second row, starting with the fourth column (B4–B7 in excel) you need to put the names of the populations each size represents as shown in https://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/Data_Preparation.html#basic-format

Genalex files have a lot of redundancy, so poppr will use that information if it's available. In your case, you specified the sizes of the populations (A4–A7), but not which populations they belong to (B4–B7)

Hope that helps!
Zhian
